correctness.rationale: Direct expansion of the Gram definition against the classical upper-half-plane Bergman kernel gives the exact quadratic auxiliary factor. Its roots are explicit and have common imaginary part with the sign of Im(xi_1/xi_0). The reciprocal-difference parameter is proved to range over the whole lower half-plane, giving both directions of the zero-free classification. Edge cases xi_1=0 and xi_0=0 are handled separately, and no numerical experiment is used.

originality.rationale: The 2026 lead source establishes the new Gram kernel and proves Lu Qi-Keng results for single-index and factorial sequences, but not for the mixed support {0,1}. Earlier xi-Bergman sources address extremal and regularity theory rather than this two-variable zero set. Targeted searches under equivalent two-coefficient and stability formulations found no implication-equivalent theorem.
residual_risks: The canonical two-variable kernel is very recent, so an unindexed independent note could contain the same quadratic calculation.
Complex-coefficient conventions require careful conjugation; the accepted proof mitigates this by deriving coefficients directly from the Gram definition.
No claim is made for support length three or larger, where higher-degree root stability can behave differently.

value.rationale: Support {0,1} is the first nontrivial finite-support family in which value and derivative evaluations interact. The exact projective phase boundary completely classifies zero-freeness for this natural family and exhibits an open failure region, giving a structural benchmark for the new Lu Qi-Keng problem rather than a routine numerical specialization.
